los.text: Perform a full gynaecological examination on a model including taking swabs and smears
los.html:
1Consent and chaperone, explain, privacy, empty bladder, position supine with knees bent and apart (or lithotomy).
2Inspect the vulva: discharge, lesions, atrophy, prolapse (ask to cough).
3. Speculum (Cusco's)
  • Warm, lubricate (water-based, away from the tip if taking smears), insert closed and sideways, rotate, open to see the cervix
  • Inspect for ectropion, polyps, lesions, discharge.
4. Swabs
  • High vaginal swab (posterior fornix: bacterial vaginosis, candida, trichomonas), endocervical swab (chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT)
  • Cervical screening (smear): brush in the os, rotate 5 times clockwise, into liquid medium.
5Close the speculum slightly as you withdraw it.
6. Bimanual (PV)Two gloved fingers in the vagina, other hand on the abdomen: cervical excitation (PID, ectopic), uterus size/position/mobility, adnexal masses or tenderness.
7Cover the patient, thank, document, chaperone's name.
  • NHS cervical screening: ages 25–64
    • HPV primary testing
    • every 3 years (25–49) and 5 years (50–64) (Wales now 5-yearly for HPV-negative 25–49).

AreaQuestions
Current pregnancy
  • LMP
  • Gestation
  • EDD (Naegele: LMP + 9 months + 7 days)
  • Planned?
  • Scans
  • Bloods
  • Symptoms (bleeding, pain, nausea, fetal movements from ~20 weeks)
Obstetric historyGravidity and parity (G/P), previous deliveries (mode, complications, birth weights), miscarriages, terminations, ectopics
Gynae historyCervical screening, contraception, fertility treatment
PMHDiabetes, hypertension, epilepsy, thyroid, mental health, VTE
DrugsFolic acid (400 µg; 5 mg if high risk), teratogens (valproate), allergies
FamilyPre-eclampsia, diabetes, genetic conditions, twins
SocialSmoking, alcohol, drugs, support, domestic abuse (ask alone), housing
  • Red flags: bleeding, abdominal pain, headache/visual disturbance (pre-eclampsia), reduced fetal movements, fluid leakage.

1Consent, chaperone, empty bladder, semi-recumbent (avoid lying flat after ~20 weeks: aortocaval compression).
2. GeneralBP (pre-eclampsia), urine dip (protein, glucose), oedema, weight/BMI.
3Inspect the abdomen: distension, scars (caesarean), striae, linea nigra, fetal movements.
4. Symphysis–fundal height (SFH)
  • Palpate the fundus with the ulnar border of the hand
  • Measure tape-side down from fundus to symphysis
  • From 24 weeks SFH in cm ≈ gestation in weeks (±2 cm)
  • Plot on a customised chart.
5. Leopold's manoeuvres(late pregnancy)Lie (longitudinal, transverse, oblique), presentation (cephalic, breech), engagement (fifths palpable).
6. Fetal heartPinard or Doppler over the anterior shoulder (110–160 bpm); feel the mother's pulse to tell them apart.

los.text: Understand principles of sexual history taking
los.html:
PrincipleDetail
Privacy and confidentialityExplain confidentiality and its limits (safeguarding)
Non-judgemental languageDon't assume sexuality or relationship status
Explain why you're asking"I ask everyone these questions"
Content
  • Symptoms (discharge, dysuria, ulcers, rash)
  • Last sexual intercourse (window periods)
  • Partners (number, gender, regular/casual, overseas)
  • Type of sex
  • Condom use
  • Contraception
  • Previous STIs
  • HIV risk (MSM, injecting drugs, high-prevalence areas)
  • PrEP
SafeguardingAge (under 16: Fraser guidelines; under 13: always safeguarding), coercion, exploitation
Partner notificationExplain why
